name: Classifier terminal with NO recorded classification → post the fallback note
description:
The fault-surfacing lane (nl-conversation-intent group 5, design D9 / semstreams HIGH-3), CORRECTED after the group-6 journeys caught it firing never. A classifier that produces NO reading must not be silent: it stamps no conversation.intent.*, so no route fires, no gate fact lands, and the human who wrote 'ship it' watches an issue where semdev appears to have ignored them. This rule posts a note pointing at the deterministic escape hatch.

THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE ABSENCE OF A RECORDED CLASSIFICATION, NOT THE LOOP OUTCOME. The shipped version keyed on agent.loop.outcome == "failed" and therefore NEVER FIRED. A tool that returns a ToolResult error does NOT fail its loop — the error goes back to the model and the loop terminates normally. So when classify_intent deliberately REFUSED to classify (the read-once binding fault: two authorized messages arrived in one poll tick, the latest-wins pending slot moved off the dispatched marker, and binding the new message's identity to a judgment of the old message's text would be exactly the misattribution D8.2 bars), the loop still ended outcome=success with iterations=1, the terminal-release rule wiped the slot, and the human was told NOTHING. Observed end-to-end, not theorized — the one-tick case now has its own journey, TestClassifierBindingFaultTellsTheHuman.

conversation.classifier.recorded is stamped by classify_intent on ITS OWN LOOP (the submit_review route-mirror shape) only when a classification actually lands. Its absence at a terminal is therefore the COMPLETE 'produced no reading' test: it covers the binding fault, a model error, a truncation, and cap exhaustion alike — every shape that leaves the human waiting. A successful classification (including a deliberate conservative `none`) stamps it and stays SILENT, because ordinary chatter must not draw a reply.

The cancelled terminal is excluded: the run itself is going away, so a note would be noise.

WHY NOT THE PARK LANE: the park rules stamp run.awaiting.human, which run-lifecycle/02 reads as a RESUME BLOCKER. Routing a classifier fault through the park would WEDGE the run — a later successful approval could never resume it. This rule stamps NOTHING and publishes user.note.<instance>, which rides the EXISTING USER stream (user.>): a note is a message to a human, not a lifecycle event (G9).

RELATIONSHIP TO 04-classifier-terminal-release: both fire on the same terminal, deliberately — 04 retires the pending slot and re-arms the spawn, this one tells the human. 04 fires on ANY terminal; this one only when no classification was recorded.

FIRING CAP: each classifier loop is a fresh entity, so this edge-triggers once per loop; the engine's default per-action cap of 3 per rule+entity is never approached.

metadata.station: classifier fault note — surface a failed classification to the human (group 5, design D9)
metadata.trigger_rationale: fires on the classifier LOOP terminal. Rule conditions read only the FIRING entity, so the run's conversation.intent.* is unreachable here — which is exactly why classify_intent mirrors conversation.classifier.recorded onto its own loop. The run id travels as the loop's agent.run.entity-id for the note consumer to resolve the thread.
metadata.no_stamp_rationale: stamps NOTHING on purpose. run.awaiting.human (the park lane's fact) is run-lifecycle/02's resume BLOCKER — parking a classifier fault would wedge the run against a later successful approval. A note is a message, not a lifecycle event.
metadata.silence_posture: a `none` (success terminal) posts nothing — ordinary chatter must not draw a reply; only a FAULT, which is indistinguishable from being ignored, is surfaced.
metadata.discriminator: absence of conversation.classifier.recorded, NOT agent.loop.outcome. A tool error does not fail its loop, so an outcome-keyed condition never fires for a refusing classifier (the shipped bug, caught by the group-6 journeys). Pinned by TestClassifierFaultPostsFallbackNote + the conflict journey.
metadata.replay_posture: DECIDED, not deferred: this rule carries NO self-extinguish marker, and that is deliberate. It publishes a human-visible comment, so on a RULE_STATE loss with ENTITY_STATES intact the engine would see hadPrevState=false → TransitionEntered and re-fire for every historically unclassified conversation loop. Three things bound it. (1) TRIGGER: RULE_STATE is created with TTL 0 / MaxBytes -1 (processor.go:568-575), so there is no routine expiry — the loss shape is operator or disaster-recovery level, not normal operation. (2) BLAST RADIUS: the note consumer suppresses the post once the run carries either gate fact, so every DECIDED run — which is every completed run — posts nothing on replay (pinned by TestFaultNoteSuppressedOnceGateDecided, both directions). The residual is runs still sitting at an undecided gate, where the note's content is still TRUE and actionable. (3) HARM: a duplicate comment, never a lifecycle effect — this rule stamps nothing. Adding a marker would buy nothing in normal operation (each classifier loop is a fresh entity that edge-triggers once) at the cost of a permanent predicate and a rule write, so the marker is NOT worth it. Revisit if the note ever gains a lifecycle effect, or if RULE_STATE loss stops being exotic.
